answers.q1: Cargo (Rust, edition 2024, MSRV 1.96). Cargo fetches dependencies as part of the build, so there is no separate install step. To fetch them explicitly, run: `cargo fetch --locked`. Or run `cargo build --workspace`, which is what CI does.
answers.q2: `cargo test --workspace`. This matches CI, which also runs it with `--features unstable-index` and `--features pcre2`. AGENTS.md gives `cargo test --all`, which is equivalent.
answers.q3: `cargo test --test it regression`. The integration target is named `it` (see `[[test]]` in Cargo.toml, path tests/tests.rs), and `regression` is a module inside it. AGENTS.md says `--test integration`, but that target doesn't exist, so that command would fail.
answers.q4: Run `cargo fmt --all --check`, then `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`. CI's rustfmt job runs both, so AGENTS.md is wrong to say there is no clippy step. CI also checks docs with `RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc --no-deps --document-private-items --workspace`. Its zsh completion check is `ci/test-complete`, which needs a built `rg` and zsh.
answers.q5: Nothing is vendored. `Cargo.lock` is generated by Cargo and shouldn't be edited by hand. `target/` holds build output and is gitignored. build.rs generates the shell completions and man page into target/. `tests/data/*` (the compressed sherlock fixtures) are fixtures that shouldn't be hand-edited. Also, `crates/core/flags/defs.rs` is the hand-edited source for the generated `--help`, man page and completions, so edit it rather than the generated output.

q1.reason: Identifies Cargo, states no separate install step, and gives `cargo fetch --locked` / `cargo build --workspace`, which match the accepted fetch/build commands.

q2.reason: Gives `cargo test --workspace`, matching CI, and notes the pcre2 variant and `cargo test --all` equivalent.

q3.reason: Gives `cargo test --test it regression`, exactly matching ACCEPT, and correctly notes `--test integration` no longer exists.

q4.reason: Gives both `cargo fmt --all --check` and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, plus the cargo doc check as a bonus.

q5.reason: Correctly says nothing is vendored and names Cargo.lock and target/, but also claims tests/data fixtures are not to be hand-edited, which conflicts with the truth that none must be hand-edited beyond Cargo.lock and target/.
